report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the resected tumor revealed a predominantly lepidic growth pattern with mucin secretion under low-power view (Fig. 1C). Middle-power magnification revealed tumor cells with abundant apical cytoplasmic mucin and small, basally oriented nuclei (Fig. 1D). The partial tumor exhibited an invasive pattern of infiltrative glands lined by tumor cells containing abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, measuring less than 5 mm in size (Fig. 1E). Notably, the focal area exhibited atypical goblet cell hyperplasia (Fig. 1F, arrows) in the bronchial epithelium (Fig. 1F, triangles). The resection margin and lymph nodes were negative.

clinician.final_diagnosis: pulmonary minimally invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (MIA, mucinous type), staged as pT1miN0M0
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 9-year-old girl presented with persistent cough and sputum production for three weeks that did not improve with antibiotic therapy. Contrast-enhanced chest CT revealed a 1.9 cm × 1.6 cm solid nodule with irregular margins and slight enhancement in the posterior basal segment of the right lower lobe. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) resection of the right lower lobe without postoperative complications. Histopathological examination confirmed mucinous adenocarcinoma with a predominantly lepidic growth pattern, abundant intracytoplasmic mucin, and an invasive component measuring less than 5 mm. Resection margins and lymph nodes were negative, supporting a final pathologic stage of pT1miN0M0.
